g.text: Chip count explains part of the compute gap, but not most of it

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: What it shows: the number of accelerators used against the compute the run produced, for every notable model that records

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: both. The spread at a given chip count is how much longer runs got, and how much faster each chip became.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: Note: 217 of 1043 notable models record both a chip count and a training compute figure; the rest are absent rather than estimated. Chip

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: count is the quantity Epoch records for the run, which for some models is the cluster size rather than the number actually used, so

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: treat the horizontal axis as an upper bound. Compute is a modelled quantity for most rows — the two axes are not independent

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: measurements, since a compute figure is sometimes derived from the hardware and the training time.
